The level of a large site is lifted 3.5 m with free-draining fill whose density is 2.05 Mg/m³. The clay's coefficient of consolidation is 2.6 m²/yr.

Neglect secondary compression. Two estimates are needed. In the first, the one-layer value takes the overburden at the clay's mid-depth. In the second the clay is cut into 6 equal parts and each sublayer takes the overburden at its own mid-depth and the same e0 and C_c. Assume ρ_w = 1.00 Mg/m³ and g = 9.81 m/s². Time factors: T = 0.197 at 50 % and T = 0.848 at 90 % average consolidation. Compute the final settlement of the 11 m clay treated whole (s_single_layer, mm) and as 6 slices (s_sublayers, mm), with t_50 and t_90 in years.

For the clay, c_v = 2.6 m²/yr from the oedometer's root-time fits. The level of a large site is lifted 3 m with free-draining fill whose density is 2.05 Mg/m³.
Before filling, water stood at the ground surface, and it stays there. Profile: 9 m of normally consolidated firm clay, saturated density 1.79 Mg/m³, compression index 0.43, void ratio 1.27, over dense, free-draining sand.

Work the settlement twice: the one-layer value takes the overburden at the clay's mid-depth; then split the clay into 6 equal sublayers, where each sublayer takes the overburden at its own mid-depth and the same e0 and C_c. Use ρ_w = 1.00 Mg/m³ and g = 9.81 m/s². Take T = 0.197 at 50 % and T = 0.848 at 90 % average consolidation. Report s_single_layer and s_sublayers for the 9 m layer, in mm; the years t_50 and t_90 to half and nine-tenths of the consolidation. Neglect secondary compression.

Consolidation tests on the clay report c_v = 1 m²/yr. Over a large area the ground is raised by 2 m of granular fill (ρ = 2.05 Mg/m³), which drains freely.
Free water lies at the base of the fill, on top of the clay. Below 10 m of soft clay the boring met dense sand that drains freely. The clay is normally consolidated, with C_c = 0.86, e0 = 1.78 and ρ_sat = 1.63 Mg/m³.

Use ρ_w = 1.00 Mg/m³ and g = 9.81 m/s² for unit weights. Then the one-layer value takes the overburden at the clay's mid-depth, and, dividing the clay into 5 slices of equal thickness, each sublayer takes the overburden at its own mid-depth and the same e0 and C_c. Time factors: T = 0.197 at 50 % and T = 0.848 at 90 % average consolidation. Report the final settlement of the 10 m clay treated whole (s_single_layer, mm) and as 5 slices (s_sublayers, mm), with t_50 and t_90 in years. Neglect secondary compression.

Its coefficient of consolidation, measured on undisturbed samples, is 1.1 m²/yr. Over a large area the ground is raised by 2 m of granular fill (ρ = 2.05 Mg/m³), which drains freely.
Piezometers put groundwater at the old surface, under the new fill. Under the fill the soft clay is normally consolidated, 10 m deep, and sits on unfissured, impervious shale; oedometer results give C_c = 0.85 and e0 = 1.7, and its saturated density is 1.68 Mg/m³.

Two estimates are needed. In the first, the one-layer value takes the overburden at the clay's mid-depth. In the second the clay is cut into 6 equal parts and each sublayer takes the overburden at its own mid-depth and the same e0 and C_c. Assume ρ_w = 1.00 Mg/m³ and g = 9.81 m/s². In the time calculation, T = 0.197 at 50 % and T = 0.848 at 90 % average consolidation. Report four values: s_single_layer and s_sublayers (mm), then t_50 and t_90 (yr) for 50 % and 90 % consolidation. Neglect secondary compression.

c_v of the clay, from laboratory tests: 1.1 m²/yr. A broad layer of pervious fill, 2.15 Mg/m³ and 3.5 m thick, is tipped onto the flat site.
The clay is saturated up to its top; the water table is at the original grade. Beneath the original surface is 8 m of soft normally consolidated clay (ρ_sat = 1.73 Mg/m³, C_c = 0.87, e0 = 1.56) lying on massive, watertight shale.

Work the settlement twice: the one-layer value takes the overburden at the clay's mid-depth; then split the clay into 4 equal sublayers, where each sublayer takes the overburden at its own mid-depth and the same e0 and C_c. Use ρ_w = 1.00 Mg/m³ and g = 9.81 m/s². Use the tabulated time factors, T = 0.197 at 50 % and T = 0.848 at 90 % average consolidation. Report how much the 8 m of clay settles by one layer and by 4 sublayers (mm), and how long it takes to reach 50 % and 90 % consolidation (t_50, t_90, yr). Neglect secondary compression.

For a new port yard, 3.5 m of crushed-rock fill of density 2 Mg/m³ is spread far beyond the area of interest; it is free-draining. Beneath the original surface is 8 m of firm normally consolidated clay (ρ_sat = 1.83 Mg/m³, C_c = 0.29, e0 = 1.03) lying on unfissured, impervious shale. Before filling, water stood at the ground surface, and it stays there. Time-settlement readings in the laboratory gave c_v of 2.6 m²/yr.

Use ρ_w = 1.00 Mg/m³ and g = 9.81 m/s² for unit weights. Then the one-layer value takes the overburden at the clay's mid-depth, and, dividing the clay into 5 slices of equal thickness, each sublayer takes the overburden at its own mid-depth and the same e0 and C_c. Time factors: T = 0.197 at 50 % and T = 0.848 at 90 % average consolidation. Neglect secondary compression. Determine s_single_layer and s_sublayers in mm, and the times t_50 and t_90 in years to 50 % and 90 % consolidation.

The clay's coefficient of consolidation is 1 m²/yr. Over a large area the ground is raised by 2 m of granular fill (ρ = 1.9 Mg/m³), which drains freely.
Before filling, water stood at the ground surface, and it stays there. Profile: 7 m of normally consolidated soft clay, saturated density 1.63 Mg/m³, compression index 1.4, void ratio 1.94, over massive, watertight shale.

Work the settlement twice: the one-layer value takes the overburden at the clay's mid-depth; then split the clay into 5 equal sublayers, where each sublayer takes the overburden at its own mid-depth and the same e0 and C_c. Use ρ_w = 1.00 Mg/m³ and g = 9.81 m/s². Use the tabulated time factors, T = 0.197 at 50 % and T = 0.848 at 90 % average consolidation. Report t_50 and t_90 in years, after the settlements s_single_layer and s_sublayers in mm. Neglect secondary compression.

The top 5.5 m is medium dense sand (γ = 17.6 kN/m³ above the water table, 19.4 kN/m³ below, φ′ = 31°). Under it lies 14 m of soft normally consolidated clay, γ_sat = 16.4 kN/m³, C_c = 0.51, e0 = 1.49, then incompressible rock. The phreatic surface is found at a depth of 2.5 m.

A grain silo pad, circular, 13 m wide and flexible, transfers 55 kPa evenly when loaded.

Neglect secondary compression. Use γ_w = 9.81 kN/m³, the exact Boussinesq stress beneath a uniformly loaded flexible circle (no influence chart), and 10 equal clay sublayers, each taking its stress increase and overburden at its mid-depth; the tank bears directly on the ground surface. Compute two settlements in mm: s_centre at the middle of the tank and s_edge at its perimeter.

Full of product, the circular tank (16 m across, flexible base) presses 50 kPa onto the soil. Profile: medium dense sand to 4.5 m with moist unit weight 17.9 kN/m³, saturated 19.4 kN/m³ and friction angle 32°; soft normally consolidated clay 18 m thick (γ_sat 16.1 kN/m³, C_c 1.14, e0 1.9); unyielding rock beneath. Below 2 m the sand is submerged.

Split the clay into 8 equal clay sublayers, each taking its stress increase and overburden at its mid-depth. Stresses: the exact Boussinesq stress beneath a uniformly loaded flexible circle (no influence chart); the tank bears directly on the ground surface. Unit weight of water: γ_w = 9.81 kN/m³. Neglect secondary compression. Determine the consolidation settlement of the clay beneath the tank centre (s_centre) and beneath its rim (s_edge), both in mm.

Planned: a flexible-bottomed tank of 16 m diameter whose contents exert 90 kPa uniformly.
Seepage into the boreholes settled at 1.5 m below ground. Soft normally consolidated clay, 16 m thick with γ_sat = 16.9 kN/m³, C_c = 0.75 and e0 = 1.61, rests on rock and is covered by 9.5 m of medium dense sand: γ = 19.3 kN/m³ dry side, 20.2 kN/m³ saturated, φ′ = 34°.

Split the clay into 8 equal clay sublayers, each taking its stress increase and overburden at its mid-depth. Stresses: the exact Boussinesq stress beneath a uniformly loaded flexible circle (no influence chart); the tank bears directly on the ground surface. Unit weight of water: γ_w = 9.81 kN/m³. Report s_centre and s_edge, the clay's consolidation settlement in mm under the centre and under the edge of the tank. Neglect secondary compression.

An oil tank with a flexible floor, 34 m in diameter, applies a uniform 65 kPa when full.
Piezometers put the water table 1.5 m down. The top 8 m is medium dense sand (γ = 19.8 kN/m³ above the water table, 20.6 kN/m³ below, φ′ = 35°). Under it lies 12 m of soft normally consolidated clay, γ_sat = 16 kN/m³, C_c = 0.84, e0 = 1.84, then incompressible rock.

Use γ_w = 9.81 kN/m³, the exact Boussinesq stress beneath a uniformly loaded flexible circle (no influence chart), and 6 equal clay sublayers, each taking its stress increase and overburden at its mid-depth; the tank bears directly on the ground surface. Report the dish of the 34 m floor: consolidation settlement at its centre, s_centre, and at its edge, s_edge (mm). Neglect secondary compression.

Profile: medium dense sand to 6.5 m with moist unit weight 20.1 kN/m³, saturated 20.6 kN/m³ and friction angle 36°; soft normally consolidated clay 16 m thick (γ_sat 16.5 kN/m³, C_c 0.84, e0 1.56); unyielding rock beneath. Seepage into the boreholes settled at 3 m below ground.

A flexible-based storage tank of diameter 37 m loads the ground uniformly with 75 kPa.

Neglect secondary compression. Split the clay into 5 equal clay sublayers, each taking its stress increase and overburden at its mid-depth. Stresses: the exact Boussinesq stress beneath a uniformly loaded flexible circle (no influence chart); the tank bears directly on the ground surface. Unit weight of water: γ_w = 9.81 kN/m³. Compute in mm, the clay's final settlement at the tank axis (s_centre) and at its circumference (s_edge).

Planned: a flexible-bottomed tank of 20 m diameter whose contents exert 100 kPa uniformly. Medium dense sand forms the first 8.5 m (17.4 kN/m³ when moist, 19.6 kN/m³ when saturated; friction angle 31°). The soft clay beneath, normally consolidated and 16 m thick, has C_c = 0.96, e0 = 1.92, γ_sat = 16.1 kN/m³. Unyielding rock follows. Piezometers put the water table 2.5 m down.

Take the exact Boussinesq stress beneath a uniformly loaded flexible circle (no influence chart); the tank bears directly on the ground surface. Divide the clay into 6 equal clay sublayers, each taking its stress increase and overburden at its mid-depth. Use γ_w = 9.81 kN/m³. Neglect secondary compression. Determine two settlements in mm: s_centre at the middle of the tank and s_edge at its perimeter.

A grain silo pad, circular, 14 m wide and flexible, transfers 85 kPa evenly when loaded. Medium dense sand forms the first 9.5 m (17.9 kN/m³ when moist, 19.6 kN/m³ when saturated; friction angle 32°). The soft clay beneath, normally consolidated and 24 m thick, has C_c = 0.68, e0 = 1.63, γ_sat = 15.9 kN/m³. Unyielding rock follows. Water stands 1 m beneath grade all year.

Assume the tank bears directly on the ground surface and γ_w = 9.81 kN/m³. For each of 8 equal clay sublayers, each taking its stress increase and overburden at its mid-depth, use the exact Boussinesq stress beneath a uniformly loaded flexible circle (no influence chart). Neglect secondary compression. Determine in mm, the clay's final settlement at the tank axis (s_centre) and at its circumference (s_edge).

An oil tank with a flexible floor, 37 m in diameter, applies a uniform 95 kPa when full. Medium dense sand forms the first 9.5 m (19.8 kN/m³ when moist, 20.7 kN/m³ when saturated; friction angle 36°). The soft clay beneath, normally consolidated and 12 m thick, has C_c = 0.87, e0 = 1.56, γ_sat = 15.9 kN/m³. Unyielding rock follows. The phreatic surface is found at a depth of 2 m.

Since the tank bears directly on the ground surface, apply the exact Boussinesq stress beneath a uniformly loaded flexible circle (no influence chart) under each point, over 6 equal clay sublayers, each taking its stress increase and overburden at its mid-depth; γ_w = 9.81 kN/m³. Neglect secondary compression. Determine in mm, the clay's final settlement at the tank axis (s_centre) and at its circumference (s_edge).

Uniform contact pressure 65 kPa acts over a circle 37 m in diameter beneath a flexible steel tank. Rock lies 27 m down. Above it: 20 m of soft clay (normally consolidated; γ_sat 15.9 kN/m³, C_c 0.86, e0 1.59), and on top 7 m of medium dense sand with φ′ 35°, weighing 19.1 kN/m³ moist and 20.1 kN/m³ saturated. Water stands 2 m beneath grade all year.

Use γ_w = 9.81 kN/m³, the exact Boussinesq stress beneath a uniformly loaded flexible circle (no influence chart), and 8 equal clay sublayers, each taking its stress increase and overburden at its mid-depth; the tank bears directly on the ground surface. Neglect secondary compression. Determine two settlements in mm: s_centre at the middle of the tank and s_edge at its perimeter.

Buildings go up after 137 mm of the settlement has happened. c_v of the clay, from laboratory tests: 0.000793 cm²/s. Over many hectares, 2 m of fill with unit weight 20.5 kN/m³ is to be laid in one stage.
Groundwater stands at the old ground level, under the fill. Beneath the site lie three strata: 3.5 m of cemented silt, dense, incompressible and practically watertight at 19.5 kN/m³, firm clay 3 m thick (normally consolidated; C_c 0.53, e0 1.25, γ_sat 17.9 kN/m³), and coarse gravel that drains freely.

Use a year of 365 days and γ_w = 9.81 kN/m³; treat the clay as one layer with its overburden at mid-depth. Take Casagrande and Taylor's approximations to the degree-time relation (U < 60 %: T = π/4 U²; U > 60 %: T = 1.781 − 0.933 log10 of 100 − U%). Report how long (t_target, yr) the ground takes to settle 137 mm, after s_ult in mm and the degree U_target as a fraction. Neglect secondary compression.

The owner may build once the ground has settled 73 mm. For the clay, c_v = 0.000793 cm²/s from the oedometer's root-time fits. The landscaping scheme raises the ground 3 m using fill of 20.5 kN/m³ over a wide plot.
The whole profile is saturated, with the water table at the original surface. Beneath the site lie three strata: 5.5 m of free-draining, dense clean sand at 19.5 kN/m³, firm clay 3.5 m thick (normally consolidated; C_c 0.36, e0 1.18, γ_sat 18.3 kN/m³), and massive impervious granite.

Here treat the clay as one layer with its overburden at mid-depth, with γ_w = 9.81 kN/m³ and a year of 365 days. Time factor from Casagrande and Taylor's approximations to the degree-time relation; below 60 % T = πU²/4, and above it T = 1.781 − 0.933·log10(100 − U%). Report the ultimate consolidation settlement s_ult in mm, the degree U_target (fraction) it has reached at the target settlement and the time t_target in years. Neglect secondary compression.

Under 4 m of dense cemented silt, practically impermeable and incompressible, saturated unit weight 20 kN/m³, the clay is normally consolidated, 5 m thick, γ_sat 19.6 kN/m³, C_c 0.34, e0 0.84; beneath it is open, water-bearing gravel. The water table is at the original ground surface.

Earthworks will place 2 m of compacted fill, 20 kN/m³, over the whole development. The owner may build once the ground has settled 48 mm. Oedometer tests give c_v = 0.000856 cm²/s for the clay.

Neglect secondary compression. Use a year of 365 days and γ_w = 9.81 kN/m³; treat the clay as one layer with its overburden at mid-depth. Take Casagrande and Taylor's approximations to the degree-time relation (U < 60 %: T = π/4 U²; U > 60 %: T = 1.781 − 0.933 log10 of 100 − U%). Compute s_ult (mm), U_target, the average degree of consolidation at the target settlement as a fraction, and t_target, the years to reach it.

Beneath the site lie three strata: 6 m of dense cemented silt, practically impermeable and incompressible at 20.5 kN/m³, firm clay 2.5 m thick (normally consolidated; C_c 0.38, e0 0.83, γ_sat 17.9 kN/m³), and coarse gravel that drains freely. The ground is saturated from the original surface downward.

A wide fill 1.5 m high (γ = 20 kN/m³) is spread over the site. Buildings go up after 15 mm of the settlement has happened. c_v of the clay, from laboratory tests: 0.000856 cm²/s.

Neglect secondary compression. For the arithmetic, γ_w = 9.81 kN/m³ and a year of 365 days; also treat the clay as one layer with its overburden at mid-depth. Relate T and U by Casagrande and Taylor's approximations to the degree-time relation: T = (π/4)U² for U below 60 %, T = 1.781 − 0.933 log10(100 − U%) above. Compute s_ult (mm), U_target, the average degree of consolidation at the target settlement as a fraction, and t_target, the years to reach it.

The ground is 5.5 m of clean dense sand, highly permeable (γ_sat = 20 kN/m³), then 6 m of firm normally consolidated clay (γ_sat = 18.4 kN/m³, C_c = 0.39, e0 = 0.95) on open, water-bearing gravel. Groundwater is at grade, so all strata below are submerged.

A uniform layer of fill, 1.5 m deep and 19 kN/m³ in unit weight, covers the entire area. Paving can start when the settlement reaches 55 mm. Consolidation tests on the clay report c_v = 0.000824 cm²/s.

Neglect secondary compression. Take γ_w = 9.81 kN/m³, a year of 365 days, and treat the clay as one layer with its overburden at mid-depth. Relate T and U by Casagrande and Taylor's approximations to the degree-time relation: T = (π/4)U² for U below 60 %, T = 1.781 − 0.933 log10(100 − U%) above. Compute the final settlement s_ult (mm), the fraction U_target of it that 55 mm represents, and t_target, the years until 55 mm is reached.

The owner may build once the ground has settled 62 mm. For the clay, c_v = 0.000761 cm²/s from the oedometer's root-time fits. A uniform layer of fill, 1.5 m deep and 19.5 kN/m³ in unit weight, covers the entire area.
Groundwater is at grade, so all strata below are submerged. Profile: hard cemented silt that neither drains nor compresses, 4 m thick with γ_sat 19 kN/m³; firm normally consolidated clay, 4 m thick, γ_sat 18.4 kN/m³, C_c = 0.4, e0 = 0.94; then a permeable gravel aquifer.

For the arithmetic, γ_w = 9.81 kN/m³ and a year of 365 days; also treat the clay as one layer with its overburden at mid-depth. For T(U) apply Casagrande and Taylor's approximations to the degree-time relation; the small-U branch is T = πU²/4, the large-U branch 1.781 − 0.933 log10(100 − U%), with 60 % the switch. Report s_ult (mm), U_target, the average degree of consolidation at the target settlement as a fraction, and t_target, the years to reach it. Neglect secondary compression.

Profile: dense cemented silt, practically impermeable and incompressible, 6 m thick with γ_sat 20 kN/m³; firm normally consolidated clay, 3 m thick, γ_sat 19.5 kN/m³, C_c = 0.26, e0 = 0.85; then coarse gravel that drains freely. The water table is at the original ground surface.

Placed across a broad area: 3 m of fill weighing 20.5 kN/m³. Buildings go up after 60 mm of the settlement has happened. For the clay, c_v = 0.000824 cm²/s from the oedometer's root-time fits.

Neglect secondary compression. Here treat the clay as one layer with its overburden at mid-depth, with γ_w = 9.81 kN/m³ and a year of 365 days. Take Casagrande and Taylor's approximations to the degree-time relation (U < 60 %: T = π/4 U²; U > 60 %: T = 1.781 − 0.933 log10 of 100 − U%). Compute the final settlement s_ult (mm), the fraction U_target of it that 60 mm represents, and t_target, the years until 60 mm is reached.

Wanted: s_ult in mm; U_target, the average degree at 111 mm of settlement as a fraction; and the elapsed time t_target in years.

Over many hectares, 1.5 m of fill with unit weight 20 kN/m³ is to be laid in one stage. Groundwater stands at the old ground level, under the fill. The ground is 5 m of dense cemented silt, practically impermeable and incompressible (γ_sat = 20.5 kN/m³), then 4 m of firm normally consolidated clay (γ_sat = 18.1 kN/m³, C_c = 0.54, e0 = 1.1) on coarse gravel that drains freely. Buildings go up after 111 mm of the settlement has happened. For the clay, c_v = 0.000729 cm²/s from the oedometer's root-time fits.

Here treat the clay as one layer with its overburden at mid-depth, with γ_w = 9.81 kN/m³ and a year of 365 days. Time factor from Casagrande and Taylor's approximations to the degree-time relation; below 60 % T = πU²/4, and above it T = 1.781 − 0.933·log10(100 − U%). Neglect secondary compression.

Survey plates must show 114 mm before slabs are cast. Time-settlement readings in the laboratory gave c_v of 0.000793 cm²/s. Placed across a broad area: 2.5 m of fill weighing 20 kN/m³.
Before and after filling, the phreatic level stays at the old surface. Profile: dense cemented silt, practically impermeable and incompressible, 4.5 m thick with γ_sat 20.5 kN/m³; firm normally consolidated clay, 3 m thick, γ_sat 18.8 kN/m³, C_c = 0.34, e0 = 0.85; then a permeable gravel aquifer.

For the arithmetic, γ_w = 9.81 kN/m³ and a year of 365 days; also treat the clay as one layer with its overburden at mid-depth. Use Casagrande and Taylor's approximations to the degree-time relation, namely T = (π/4)·U² up to U = 60 % and T = 1.781 − 0.933 log10(100 − U%) beyond. Report s_ult in mm; U_target, the average degree at 114 mm of settlement as a fraction; and the elapsed time t_target in years. Neglect secondary compression.

Finishes tolerate 23 mm of settlement at most. Square spread footing: B = 3.2 m, base at 0.9 m depth; one trial net pressure of 290 kPa is to be checked.
Borings stayed dry to well past the influence depth. Two sands: an upper loose one, γ = 17 kN/m³ and E_s = 21 MPa, ending 4 m below the base, and a dense one under it with E_s = 54.5 MPa. The same loose sand lies between grade and the base.

Apply Schmertmann's modified method with the stated E_s values with no further multiplier and eight sublayers B/4 thick from the base to 2B, I_z taken at each centre. Here I_z rises from 0.1 at the base to I_zp at depth B/2 below it and falls to zero at 2B, I_zp = 0.5 + 0.1√(Δp/σ′_vp), σ′_vp the effective overburden at depth B/2 below the base, C1 = 1 − 0.5σ′_v0/Δp, not less than 0.5 and C2 = 1. Report settlement_at_q (mm) for 290 kPa, then q_allow_settlement (kPa) for the 23 mm limit. Neglect secondary compression.

Finishes tolerate 22 mm of settlement at most. Footing geometry: width 2.2 m (square), founding depth 0.8 m. Initial net loading to test: 120 kPa.
The sands are dry throughout the zone that matters. CPT soundings show loose sand (16.8 kN/m³; E_s about 15.5 MPa) to 2.75 m beneath the founding level and dense sand (E_s 54.5 MPa) deeper. Above the founding level the ground is that loose sand too.

Discretise into eight sublayers B/4 thick from the base to 2B, I_z taken at each centre and apply Schmertmann's modified method, with the stated E_s values with no further multiplier; C2 = 1, C1 = 1 − 0.5σ′_v0/Δp, not less than 0.5; I_zp = 0.5 + 0.1√(Δp/σ′_vp), σ′_vp the effective overburden at depth B/2 below the base; the shape: I_z rises from 0.1 at the base to I_zp at depth B/2 below it and falls to zero at 2B. Report q_allow_settlement in kPa, the net pressure giving 22 mm, and settlement_at_q, the mm of settlement under 120 kPa. Neglect secondary compression.

Wanted: q_allow_settlement in kPa, the net pressure giving 17 mm, and settlement_at_q, the mm of settlement under 270 kPa.

A square footing 3 m wide is founded 1.1 m below grade. The first loading checked is a net pressure Δp = 270 kPa. The water table is far below the zone of influence. Dense sand, E_s 52.5 MPa, starts 3 m under the footing base; above it is loose sand with E_s 28 MPa and γ 19.6 kN/m³. The embedment is in the loose sand as well. Settlement is limited to 17 mm.

Discretise into eight sublayers B/4 thick from the base to 2B, I_z taken at each centre and apply Schmertmann's modified method, with the stated E_s values with no further multiplier; C2 = 1, C1 = 1 − 0.5σ′_v0/Δp, not less than 0.5; I_zp = 0.5 + 0.1√(Δp/σ′_vp), σ′_vp the effective overburden at depth B/2 below the base; the shape: I_z rises from 0.1 at the base to I_zp at depth B/2 below it and falls to zero at 2B. Neglect secondary compression.

A pad of 2.9 m square bears at 2 m. Its net applied pressure is first taken as 150 kPa. Two sands: an upper loose one, γ = 15.2 kN/m³ and E_s = 12.5 MPa, ending 2.175 m below the base, and a dense one under it with E_s = 76.5 MPa. Above the founding level the ground is that loose sand too. Borings stayed dry to well past the influence depth. The allowable settlement is 21 mm.

By Schmertmann's modified method (C2 = 1; C1 = 1 − 0.5σ′_v0/Δp, not less than 0.5): I_z rises from 0.1 at the base to I_zp at depth B/2 below it and falls to zero at 2B, and I_zp = 0.5 + 0.1√(Δp/σ′_vp), σ′_vp the effective overburden at depth B/2 below the base. Sum over eight sublayers B/4 thick from the base to 2B, I_z taken at each centre, taking the stated E_s values with no further multiplier. Neglect secondary compression. Determine q_allow_settlement in kPa, the net pressure giving 21 mm, and settlement_at_q, the mm of settlement under 150 kPa.

Wanted: settlement_at_q, the settlement in mm under the trial pressure, and q_allow_settlement, the largest net pressure in kPa that keeps the settlement to the limit.

Under a net pressure of 110 kPa, a square footing 3.1 m wide founded at 1.7 m is examined first. Water lies deep enough to be ignored. Dense sand, E_s 60.5 MPa, starts 2.325 m under the footing base; above it is loose sand with E_s 23.5 MPa and γ 19.1 kN/m³. Loose sand also forms the soil from the surface down to the base. Specification: settlement of 17 mm or less.
